stem: Researchers identify a family with an inherited insulin gene mutation that causes a single amino acid substitution in proinsulin.  Affected family members have normal blood glucose levels, and their mature insulin is structurally identical to normal human insulin.  The researchers conclude that the amino acid substitution affects the segment of proinsulin that connects the insulin A and B chains and is removed during post-translational processing of the protein.  Which of the following is the most likely fate of the polypeptide segment containing the mutation?​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌

options.label: C
options.text: Degradation in the rough endoplasmic reticulum

options.label: D
options.text: Direct translocation from the cytosol across the plasma membrane

explanation:
The segment of proinsulin that connects the insulin A and B chains is C-peptide, so the mutation in this family lies within C-peptide.  C-peptide does not contribute to the glucose-lowering effects of insulin, and normal mature insulin structure and blood glucose levels indicate that the mutant proinsulin was folded and processed normally.  Therefore, the substitution causes no symptoms, and the mutant C-peptide follows the same pathway as normal C-peptide:

  • Insulin is synthesized by pancreatic beta cells as preproinsulin, a precursor with a hydrophobic N-terminal signal peptide.  Translation begins on a free cytosolic ribosome; as the signal peptide emerges, it binds a signal recognition particle (SRP), which halts translation until the ribosome docks on the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). 
  • Once bound to the RER, translation resumes and the growing peptide chain is extruded into the RER lumen.  The N-terminal signal peptide is cleaved (and subsequently degraded) to yield proinsulin, which undergoes conformational changes and the formation of 3 disulfide bonds in the RER. 
  • Proinsulin is transported to the Golgi apparatus, where it is packaged into secretory granules.  Proteolytic enzymes in the secretory granules cleave proinsulin into insulin (A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds) and C-peptide.  Insulin and C-peptide are stored within the granules until they are secreted together by exocytosis in equimolar amounts.

C-peptide is a marker of endogenous insulin secretion; exogenous insulin preparations do not contain C-peptide.  C-peptide also undergoes minimal hepatic extraction and has a longer half-life than insulin (20–30 min vs 3–5 min), so its serum level more reliably reflects beta-cell output.

(Choice A)  Lysosomes primarily degrade extracellular material taken up by endocytosis and intracellular components delivered by autophagy (eg, damaged organelles).  Normally processed C-peptide is predominantly secreted with insulin rather than degraded in lysosomes.

(Choices B and C)  Proteins that misfold in the RER are not degraded there; instead, they are retrotranslocated into the cytosol, ubiquitinated, and degraded by proteasomes (ER-associated degradation).  Some insulin gene mutations cause proinsulin misfolding, which impairs insulin production and causes diabetes.  In this family, normal insulin production indicates that the substitution did not impair folding.

(Choice D)  A few secretory proteins (eg, interleukin-1β) lack a signal sequence and are secreted directly from the cytosol by unconventional mechanisms.  In contrast, C-peptide is part of proinsulin, which has a signal peptide, so C-peptide follows the conventional RER-Golgi pathway and is released by exocytosis.

Educational objective:Cleavage of proinsulin in pancreatic beta-cell secretory granules yields insulin and C-peptide, which are stored in the granules until they are secreted in equimolar amounts.​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​​​​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌
